text.p: Volkswagen AG said Tuesday that its group earnings more than doubled last year as sales expanded by 14 percent.

The company said profit at the group level rose by 102 percent to 678 million marks ($404.5 million) from 336 million marks ($200.5 million) while earnings at the parent level rose 54 percent to 630 million marks ($375.9 million) from 410 million marks ($244.6 million).
It added that sales rose to 100.1 billion marks ($59.7 billion).
But the carmaker said cash flow, viewed by analysts as a more reliable reflection of VW's financial health, rose a meagre 4.4 percent to 10.85 billion marks ($6.5 billion).
The carmaker has been famous in the investment community for providing limited information about its books and profit figures have long been considered heavily influenced by provisions and taxes.
VW also said it would propose to its supervisory board that the dividend on 1996 results for ordinary shares be raised to nine marks ($5.37) from six marks ($3.58).

Stock traders were unimpressed by the results, saying the profit figures were below market expectations and shares in Volkswagen slipped by 5 marks ($2.98) to 791 marks ($471.95) in after-hours electronic trading.
